name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply formatting-only patches to third-party dependencies.

This keeps our codebase clean without risking logic changes. The trade-off is we won’t catch deeper issues in dependencies, but that’s better handled by dedicated security tools. It’s safe, fast, and directly improves readability.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "skipping deeper logic fixes"—it’s that formatting-only patches mask dependency rot by treating symptoms, not causes. A better alternative: auto-apply *only* when tests pass, then log the diff for human review. Settle it by running a pilot on one dependency and measuring how often tests catch hidden issues.
